items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Terminology 10:1
items.html: (To the question) What are the two general pregnancies of the externality? There are three general pregnancies, and they correspond to the three general ascents of ZA — to the general Neshama, Chaya, and Yechida within him. And the first general pregnancy is for the Mochin of the general Neshama, which are the Mochin of YESHSUT, which prevail on weekdays, by which ZA ascends up to the chest of AA and attains his general Neshama. And the second general pregnancy is for the Mochin of the general Chaya, which are the Mochin of the upper Aba and Ima, which prevail on Shabbat at Musaf, when ZA ascends and clothes up to the crown of Aba and Ima, which is the throat of AA, and attains his general Chaya. And the third general pregnancy is for his Mochin of Yechida, which are the Mochin of the GAR of AA, which prevail on Shabbat at Mincha, when ZA ascends and clothes the GAR of AA. And here the first two pregnancies, for the Neshama and the Chaya, are called the two general pregnancies of the externality of ZA. And only the third pregnancy is called the pregnancy of the internality of ZA.
